series: From a handbook to a Nobel (Part 1 of 3)
hook: A 1,600-year-old first-aid book won a Nobel Prize.
idea: Tu Youyou found the clue to artemisinin in Ge Hong's 4th-century handbook: soak qinghao in cold water, don't boil it.
explanation: Her team's extracts kept failing. The old recipe said cold water. Heat was destroying the active compound, so they switched to low-temperature extraction and it worked.

visual.direction: Slate background, Bone serif text, one hand-drawn wormwood sprig in Ember line art; frame 0 shows the hook in full.

caption:
In the 1970s a Chinese pharmacologist reread a 4th-century first-aid handbook and noticed one word: cold.

That word led to artemisinin, now a frontline malaria drug, and a Nobel Prize in 2015 (Tu, Nature Medicine 2011).

Part 2 on Thursday: why the method mattered more than the plant.

Historical interest only, not medical advice. Some traditional remedies are toxic.
